State of Karnataka]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj held that the BBMP (now Greater Bengaluru Authority) owed a statutory and public duty in relation to the tree even though it stood within the premises of a private school. items.title: Karnataka High Court permits man to donate kidney altruistically to unrelated recipient; State to frame guidelines
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday permitted a 52-year-old bachelor to donate one of his kidneys altruistically to a deserving, unrelated recipient. Justice Suraj Govindaraj passed the order after taking note of a medical report submitted by the Institute of Nephro Urology at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru. Pertinently, the State government informed the Court that it is framing guidelines laying down a mechanism for dealing with cases of altruistic organ donation. Justice Suraj Govindraj The petitioner had approached the High Court seeking permission to donate one of his kidneys to a deserving recipient without seeking any monetary consideration or other benefit. The petitioner told the Court that he is a bachelor who has been living independently for more than 16 years. His mother and brother are his close family members, but neither is dependent on him. The petitioner expressed his willingness to donate one of his kidneys to any deserving recipient, irrespective of caste, religion, financial status or personal relationship, while maintaining confidentiality regarding the identities of the donor and recipient. items.title: Karnataka High Court forms 3-judge panel to assess feasibility of more HC benches
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Tuesday constituted a three-member committee to examine the feasibility of establishing circuit or permanent benches of High Court at Mangaluru, Udupi, Shivamogga, Chikkamagaluru, Kodagu-Madikeri, Hassan, Davanagere and Uttara Kannada. The committee was constituted by the Chief Justice through a notification dated September 29. The three-member panel comprises Justice Anu Sivaraman , Justice SG Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz . Justice Anu Sivaraman, Justice S G Pandit and Justice Mohammad Nawaz The notification states that the committee has been constituted to verify the feasibility of establishing a High Court circuit bench/permanent bench in the identified regions. The committee has also been directed to consult all stakeholders before submitting its report to the High Court on the feasibility of establishing such benches. The notification, issued by Registrar General M Chandrashekar Reddy, states that the committee will function with immediate effect. The issue assumes significance since Karnataka currently has the principal seat at Bengaluru and benches at Dharwad and Kalaburagi. items.title: Kavin caste murder: HC quashes chargesheet against parents, finds no proof they met accused
items.summary: The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday, September 29, quashed the chargesheet against Saravanan and Krishnakumari, the parents of Surjith, the main accused in the murder of 27-year-old IT employee C Kavin Selvaganesh in Tirunelveli in July 2025. The court, however, dismissed a petition filed by Surjith’s relative Jayapal, who had sought to quash the chargesheet against him. The order was passed by Justice R Vijayakumar of the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court. Kavin, who belonged to a Scheduled Caste community and hailed from Arumugamangalam in Thoothukudi district, was hacked to death in Tirunelveli’s KTC Nagar on July 27, 2025. Surjith, the younger brother of Kavin’s partner S Subhashini, was arrested in connection with the murder. Kavin’s relationship with Subhashini was opposed by her family because of the caste difference. Kavin belonged to the Devendra Kula Vellalar community, which is a Scheduled Caste in Tamil Nadu, while Subhashini’s family is from the Maravar sub-caste of the Thevar community. items.title: Delhi High Court constitutes committee under ex-CJI Sanjiv Khanna to oversee Greenopolis homebuyers’ claims

Former Delhi Higher Judicial Service (DHJS) officers HS Sharma and Ajay Kumar Kuhar will assist Justice Khanna in the committee. Justice Khanna has offered to work pro bono. It asked the Justice Khanna committee to endeavour to complete its work within eight months of its first meeting and submit reports every three months. items.title: From 'just one more' to 'buy the whole damn pack': Allahabad High Court judge writes poem on dangers of smoking
items.summary: Justice Shekhar B Saraf of Allahabad High Court has written a poem to highlight the dangers of smoking. Justice Saraf annexed the poem to a judgment delivered by him and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary on Tuesday on the illegality of serving hookah in the restaurants in Uttar Pradesh . "From my own experience of smoking, I pen these last paragraphs in an attempt to educate the young generation of this country to not become a prey to the deleterious and indelible habit of tobacco smoking," Justice Saraf said. The judge writes that he was an unwilling smoker in the beginning but it soon turned into a habit. The “occasional” ‘sutta’ soon grew bold, It multiplied like rabbits, unrestrained." The judge went on to highlight how smoking became a norm for him. items.title: Delhi High Court slaps ₹1 lakh costs on advocate for attending hearing from moving car
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on an advocate for appearing in a virtual hearing from a moving car. Justice Om Prakash Shukla observed that the convenience of virtual proceedings cannot come at the cost of courtroom decorum or cause disturbance in the conduct of judicial proceedings. "When this Court has to deal with more than 70 matters in a day, background noise and movement during the hearing are disruptive for this Court to proceed," the Bench said. Justice Om Prakash Shukla It added that even the High Court's Electronic Evidence and Video Conferencing Rules, 2025 state that an endeavour shall be made by advocates not to join proceedings from vehicles, except in exceptional circumstances and with the permission of the Court. "The requirement is not merely procedural and to ensure that even when Counsel appear virtually, they do so from an environment conducive to the proper functioning of this Court. There is no such exceptional circumstances existing in the present matter and the conduct of the Counsel is in violation of the rules," the Court said.
